subject: DPA visibility exception request — Aurelia telemetry exports & subprocessor allowlist
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 23 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Aurelia DPA redlines — visibility & subprocessors (first pass)

Priya — looping you in.

Aurelia (prospect moving to pilot) sent back a DPA with three notable asks that need Product + Security input before Legal will accept: 1) a clause allowing aggregate telemetry exports to an external analytics vendor for ROI analysis, 2) an explicit subprocessor allowlist (they want MetricFlow and CortexMetrics allowed), and 3) a runtime visibility carveout that would permit short-lived KV/trace snapshots to be persisted for 30 days for troubleshooting.

Key context: this is a time-limited pilot (6 months) with potential to convert to Dedicated if performance/controls are required. They flagged the window as a gating item — procurement wants a sign-off by EOD Friday so they can include it in the commercial redline.

Attached: Aurelia_DPA_redlines_v1.pdf (their marked-up DPA).

Can Product/Security confirm whether any of these are showstoppers and what mitigation language we should propose? High-level asks:
- Is exporting aggregated telemetry to a third party acceptable with our current telemetry pipeline?
- Can we provide an allowlist for subprocessors, and what minimum evidence do we require from those vendors?
- Is 30-day retention of runtime snapshots feasible, or do we need to push back to a shorter window?

Thanks — happy to summarize for Legal after we align.

— Olga
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Thanks Olga — I read their redlines and pulled out the specific asks below. Quoting your note for context.

On Tue, May 23, 2028 at 9:12 AM Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com> wrote:
> Priya — looping you in.
>
> Aurelia (prospect moving to pilot) sent back a DPA with three notable asks that need Product + Security input before Legal will accept: 1) a clause allowing aggregate telemetry exports to an external analytics vendor for ROI analysis, 2) an explicit subprocessor allowlist (they want MetricFlow and CortexMetrics allowed), and 3) a runtime visibility carveout that would permit short-lived KV/trace snapshots to be persisted for 30 days for troubleshooting.
>
> Key context: this is a time-limited pilot (6 months) with potential to convert to Dedicated if performance/controls are required.

From Product perspective I need quick answers to these items so I can scope product work and state trade-offs to the customer: 
1) Telemetry exports: Is it possible to produce only aggregated, non-tokenized usage/latency/error metrics (no raw prompts or outputs) and push to an external S3 bucket maintained by Aurelia or their analytics partner? What footprint & config changes would that require?
2) Subprocessor allowlist: We can run an allowlist process but Product/Sec must define the minimum evidence (SOC2, Data Processing Agreement with subproc, encryption at rest). Will Security accept a conditional allowlist pending vendor evidence?
3) Runtime snapshots: 30 days is long. What are the platform risks and operational cost of increasing retention from our standard 7 days to 30?

Requested: Laura & Dev — please reply with short bullets (risk, feasibility, rough timeline or alternative language) so I can forward to Legal + Sales. Olga — I will prepare a two-option proposal for Aurelia (1 = allowed exports + strict evidence gating; 2 = deny exports but offer Dedicated pilot + expanded telemetry in-host).

— Priya
Head of Product Ops (Privacy & Compliance)
Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 24 May 2028 11:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Aurelia DPA redlines — visibility & subprocessors (first pass)

Priya — quick technical read:

Thanks for the clear breakdown. Short answers below.

1) Telemetry exports (aggregated only) — feasible. Our ingestion pipeline already generates aggregated metrics (per-route QPS, latency P50/95, error rates). Delivering these to an external S3 is doable, but we must ensure no raw prompt/output or raw token traces are included in the export artifact. Implementation effort: 2 engineer-weeks to add export sink + config-driven selectors; plus 1 week for secure transfer/authz to Aurelia's S3 (IAM role or pre-signed object flow). If Legal insists on sample traces removed, we can apply sampling + hashing in the pipeline; that adds another 1 week.

2) Subprocessor allowlist — operationally simple to maintain as a per-account config. However, we require Security sign-off before adding vendors. For MetricFlow/CortexMetrics we need evidence: SOC2 Type II (or equivalent), an executed DPA with that vendor, and encryption-at-rest documentation.

3) Runtime snapshots 30-day retention — higher risk. Our current default is 7 days; increasing to 30 days increases storage (approx +3.5x for per-account short-lived snapshots) and expands blast radius for PII exposure. If we must accommodate 30 days, recommend: (a) pseudonymize direct user content in snapshots (hash identifiers), (b) restrict access to a dedicated ops role with audit logging, (c) limit snapshot resolution (no full token stream) to reduce size. Estimated effort: 3–4 engineer-weeks to add retention config + pseudonymization + RBAC/audit hooks.

If Product prefers a faster path: propose Dedicated pilot (private tenancy) where we can offer 30-day retention under stricter access controls without changing the hosted default. That avoids product-wide risk.

— Dev
Engineering Lead, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 25 May 2028 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Aurelia DPA redlines — visibility & subprocessors (first pass)

Thanks team — summarized decision + next steps for Legal/Customer.

Summary (Security position):
- Telemetry exports: conditional approval. We will allow aggregated metrics exports ONLY if: (i) exports contain no raw prompts/outputs, (ii) exports are schema-validated to exclude token-level data, (iii) we receive vendor evidence (SOC2 Type II + executed DPA) for MetricFlow and CortexMetrics before enabling any exports to them.
- Subprocessor allowlist: acceptable as a per-account allowlist with Security gating. Legal must insert explicit language that Redwood will not add a subprocessor to the customer's allowlist until Security confirms evidence and Legal executes a DPA with the subprocessor.
- Runtime snapshots: cannot approve 30-day retention for hosted accounts by default. Options: (a) Offer a Dedicated pilot (private tenancy) with 30-day retention and RBAC/audit controls; (b) If customer insists on hosted retention, approve 14 days max with mandatory pseudonymization and strict ops access + audit logging. 30 days is a material increase in risk for hosted.

Attachments: security_evidence_checklist.xlsx (checklist for vendor evidence we require).

Action items: 
1) Priya — please prepare two redline options for Legal to send to Aurelia: (Option A) Aggregated export allowed + vendor gating + hosted retention capped at 14 days with pseudonymization; (Option B) Dedicated pilot with 30-day retention and full RBAC/audit controls.
2) Olga — please ask Aurelia to confirm whether they prefer Hosted+controls or Dedicated pilot. Also request MetricFlow/CortexMetrics SOC2 evidence and the contact for procurement.
3) Legal — (cc omitted here) prepare a DPA clause that references the allowlist gating language and includes the timeline for vendor evidence.

If we get vendor evidence this week we can turn on exports for the pilot before the pilot start, otherwise default to Dedicated option for the timeline.

— Laura
Director, Product Security
Redwood Inference
